moat_against: Identical SKUs sold by Amazon/Walmart/Costco — price transparency, price-matching, no pricing power
Amazon took #1 US consumer-electronics spending share in 2025 (~31% vs ~27%)
Manufacturers set product economics and can sell direct
Structurally thin ~4% operating margin leaves no downturn buffer; appliances contested by Home Depot/Lowe's
moat_for: Geek Squad services/installation and in-store expertise online rivals cannot match
~1,068-store showroom + same-day pickup network, prohibitively expensive to replicate
Vendor partnerships and store-within-store concepts with exclusive launches/demos
High-margin adjuncts growing: Best Buy Ads (~10% guided growth) and Marketplace (FY27 GMV forecast raised to $1.3B)
moat_justification: Durable #1 US specialty consumer-electronics position held for over a decade, with a Geek Squad service/installation network and ~1,000-store showroom/pickup footprint nobody would fund building today, plus growing ads and marketplace adjuncts. But it sells identical manufacturer-branded SKUs against Amazon (which passed it to ~31% of US CE spending in 2025 vs BBY ~27%), Walmart and Costco with full price transparency and no pricing power; manufacturers set product economics; the category is replacement-driven with negative 3y/5y revenue CAGRs; and operating margins are structurally capped around 4%. Real position, no pricing power — 4/10.
name: Best Buy Co., Inc.
one_liner: Durable #1 specialty CE retailer, moat 4/10, quality cash generation — but at $94.18 it prices in a recovery the numbers don't pay for: weighted IRR 10.2%, IV@15% $58.27; clears 15% only at ~$58 or below (method range D–C across median/TTM bases).
